title: Tiered capacity hedge and conversion-scaling workbook
summary: Working workbook that couples a tiered capacity hedge (reserved vs burst GPU mix) with conversion and pricing sensitivity to produce hiring triggers and runway delta scenarios. Intentionally compact; meant for weekly finance + sales sync and ops planning.
content:
TIERED CAPACITY HEDGE & CONVERSION-SCALING WORKBOOK — DRAFT

Context and goal:
- Build a small, auditable model that maps pricing moves and conversion outcomes to concrete headcount and capacity reserve actions.
- Provide clear triggers for: (A) pause hires, (B) accelerate hires, (C) switch capacity between reserved and burst.
- Focus window: Jul 2026 — Dec 2026 (6 months).

Key assumptions (conservative baseline):
- Baseline ARR churn/seasonality ignored for short window; model driven by usage conversion.
- Current committed capacity: 200 reserved GPU-hours equivalent per day (normalized).
- Burst capacity available: up to 1.8x baseline at premium cost.
- Average revenue per converted seat (ARPC): $1,200/mo baseline.
- Token-driven variable cost per converted request average: $0.0009/token.
- Average tokens per converted session: 4,200 tokens.
- Hiring lead-time (SWE/ML): 8 weeks; Ops hires: 4 weeks.

HEADCOUNT PLAN (by month, hires planned vs net add) — simplified table (roles, net headcount add):
Role, Jul-26, Aug-26, Sep-26, Oct-26, Nov-26, Dec-26
Senior SWE, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0
ML Infra Eng, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0
SRE/Oncall, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0
Solutions Eng (CS enable), 1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0
Finance / Capacity Planner (temp), 0, 1 (contract), 0, 0, 0, 0
Total net adds, 2, 3, 2, 1, 0, 0

Assumed fully-loaded monthly cost per hire (USD):
- Senior SWE: $26,000
- ML Infra Eng: $22,000
- SRE: $18,000
- Solutions Eng: $15,000
- Temp finance: $9,000

MONTHLY COST RUN-RATE IMPACT (approx) = sum(role_count * cost) + incremental capacity spend.

PRICING & CONVERSION SENSITIVITY (scenarios):
- Baseline price (P0): current public tier (no change). Conversion rate (CR) baseline = 3.6% trial->paid; take-rate of product-led funnel = 0.8% of MAU.
- Scenario A (soft discount -5%): Elasticity observed = +12% conversion relative to baseline; take-rate uplifts slightly; avg revenue per conversion falls by 5%.
- Scenario B (price increase +7%): Elasticity = -18% conversion; revenue per conversion +7%.
- Scenario C (feature-bundling, targeted discount for high-token customers): Conversion +30% in targeted segments; overall revenue weighted change = +4%.

Sensitivity table (summary view):
Scenario, % price delta, conv delta, net rev delta (month), expected token volume delta, effect on monthly burn (USD), runway delta (months)
Baseline, 0%, 0%, 0%, 0%, 0, 0
A: -5% discount, -5%, +12% conv, -3% net rev, +8% tokens, +$42,000, -0.9
B: +7% raise, +7%, -18% conv, -12% net rev, -14% tokens, -$58,000 (cost reduction), +1.2
C: targeted bundle, variable, +30% conv (segment), +4% net rev overall, +20% tokens (segment), +$18,000, -0.4
Notes: runway delta relative to current 11.4 months runway (post Q2 closes). Positive runway delta means runway increases. Scenario A increases usage (tokens) so variable cost grows; net effect reduces runway. Scenario B reduces usage and marginally improves runway but risks signups. Scenario C is highest upside for revenue with controlled cost if targeted correctly.

CAPACITY HEDGE (reserved vs burst economics):
- Reserved cost equivalent per effective GPU-hour: $6.10/hr (amortized, fixed).
- Burst (on-demand) marginal cost equivalent per GPU-hour: $12.75/hr.
- Rule-of-thumb hedge bands: keep reserved at 75-90% of steady-state demand for predictable SLOs; allow burst to cover 10-25% peak.

Cost impact example (monthly):
- Steady-state demand = 6,000 GPU-hours/mo. Reserved cover 4,500 (75%); burst 1,500.
- Reserved monthly = 4,500 * 24 * 30? (we use normalized daily-equivalent) [we show normalized calc below].
Normalized simplified calc: reserve_hours * effective_cost = 4,500 * $6.10 = $27,450 / month; burst_hours * cost = 1,500 * $12.75 = $19,125 / month. Total infra = $46,575/mo.

If Scenario A increases token volume +8% -> GPU-hours ~ +7.5% -> extra infra = $3,493/mo on burst mix unless we convert reserved ahead of time. Converting 10% more capacity to reserved adds committed fixed cost but reduces marginal per-hour. Breakeven horizon for additional reservation approx 4 months under expected run rate uplift.

DECISION TRIGGERS (hard):
- Hiring pause: if monthly net revenue delta < -6% for three consecutive weeks AND GAAP runway reduces by >0.6 months, freeze non-essential SWE hiring.
- Accelerate hiring: if sustained conversion lift > +14% for 6 weeks and gross margin contribution from incremental cohort > 40% within 90 days, greenlight 2x SWE and 1x Solutions Eng early.
- Reserve-buy: if projected burst spend > 18% of infra budget for next 90 days and expected uplift persists > 3 months, purchase additional reserved tranche (minimum 3 month commitment).
- Contract temp finance: if runway sensitivity scenario shows a data gap > 6 percentage points between modeled and observed conversion, bring temp finance immediately (lead time < 2 weeks).

EXAMPLE CALC WALKTHROUGH (short):
1) Observe weekly conversion: 4-week trailing conversion = 4.3% (baseline 3.6%).
2) Map to customers converted -> incremental ARR subtotal = 45 customers * $1,200 = $54k/month.
3) Estimate token inflation = +11% against baseline -> variable cost +$5,900/mo.
4) Net contribution = $54k - $5.9k - incremental hiring ramp (if chosen) -> available for fixed costs and runway.

SHEET TABS (recommended organization):
- T0 Assumptions (this sheet)
- T1 Headcount plan & cashflow (detailed per role, start date, salary, on-target comms, hire fill probability)
- T2 Pricing scenarios (sensitivity matrices, cohort elasticities)
- T3 Capacity hedge (reserved vs burst utilization and amortization)
- T4 Decision triggers (binary logic and notification owners)
- T5 Audit log (change history + linked PRs/tickets)

OPEN QUESTIONS / ITEMS FOR NEXT WEEK:
- Get engineering estimates: normalized GPU-hours per 1k converted sessions for gen-embedding vs chat-heavy flows (jira: JIRA-MLINF-206).
- Confirm take-rate segmentation: enterprise vs self-serve; we need per-segment elasticity numbers (owner: Sofia).
- Run sensitivity with 3-month committed buy vs pay-as-you-go to compute 3-6 month cash delta for a 15% uplift scenario (owner: Priya).

ACTION ITEMS / OWNERSHIP:
- Priya: formalize T1 cashflow tab and model hire fill probabilities (due Jun 9).
- Noah: feed actual GPU billing last 8 weeks into T3 (due Jun 4).
- Sofia: gather conversion by cohort (trial length, product route) and produce per-cohort elasticity priors (due Jun 11).
- Evan: surface any active enterprise negotiations that could change committed revenue assumptions (ongoing).

NOTES / AUDIT:
- This workbook intentionally uses conservative break-even windows (4 months) to avoid over-committing reserved capacity when conversion spikes are transient.
- We are modelling headcount as probabilistic hires (fill rates: 80% default) to capture hiring risk.

End of workbook snapshot.

Revision history: v0.1 (2026-05-10) initial draft by Priya; v0.2 (2026-05-27) added pricing sensitivity rows and reserved calc; v0.3 (2026-06-02) updated decision triggers and added owners.
